speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This includes activities by foreign companies with operations in Singapore, such as Ubisoft and Bandai Namco, as well as local firms, such as Sea and GoGame.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: On the community engagement front, events such as e-sports tournaments have also been organised in the heartlands to bring our youths together.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: An example is the "Yio Game On" event, that was organised at Yio Chu Kang Community Club in May this year, which was well-received.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Government agencies have been supporting local startups and companies in this space.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Sea, formerly known as Garena, is one of Singapore's unicorns and first made its mark through its platform for video games.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The games industry has also catalysed the growth of other companies in the ecosystem, such as Razer and Secretlab, which are globally prominent lifestyle brands amongst gamers today.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are building on such successes through several approaches.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, we are helping our companies to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In addition, companies can leverage sector-specific initiatives, such as the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA's) PIXEL innovation space, which offers incubation and co-working spaces for digital startups so they can develop their projects with the right technical and business support.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are building a robust talent pipeline for the video games industry.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Local games schools, such as DigiPen Institute and Nanyang Polytechnic, offer courses for aspiring game designers and artists to develop their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: IMDA also works with the Economic Development Board (EDB) to attract internationally-acclaimed studios, providing a platform for our entrepreneurs to gain valuable experience before starting their own studios.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Third, we are building a vibrant and enabling ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, game engine company Unity Technologies has been supporting gaming startups at PIXEL with mentorship, workshops and technical support since 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This ecosystem has supported companies like BattleBrew Productions, founded by a DigiPen graduate, and whose first mobile game intellectual property (IP) won the Visitor’s Choice Award at the GameStart Asia 2018 convention.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: During our Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Chairmanship last year, the first ASEAN e-sports and music festival, Hyperplay, was held in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The event was well-attended by over 8,000 youths of different backgrounds and featured the first League of Legends ASEAN tournament.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Gamescom is the world’s largest video games industry event and business platform.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Singapore edition will also let our video games companies showcase their capabilities and connect with prospective investors, collaborators and buyers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Singapore Tourism Board will continue to be on the lookout for other major events which can be hosted in Singapore, to further augment our position as a video games and e-sports hub in the region.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just a few supplementary questions in relation to electronic game development and e-sports.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What avenues and platforms are available for Singaporeans to get postgraduate training?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because in order to develop sophisticated and successful games, postgraduate training in the necessary skills should be available.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I know some big multinational companies do provide training.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that, in general, this training is provided to their own employees and it is not open-sourced and available to everyone.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, what are the avenues that are available for postgraduate training?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, what has been the trend in the grants given and what has been the success associated with that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly and lastly, is support given to game developers to market their own games directly to customers independently of a publisher?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I ask this because a game development company can go through a publisher in order to market their game, and the publisher then takes a large part of the margin.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That is value that otherwise the game development company could capture.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is support given to game development companies and, if necessary, grants?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Are they given without requiring them to be allied to a publisher, to be endorsed by a publisher, to work with the publisher, but instead just encourage them to actually market their games directly to customers through platforms like Steam or App Store or so on and, therefore, capture a lot more value and become more financially self-sustaining?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Whether we start any postgraduate course, whether for e-sports or any other thing, depends on the demand for the course and curriculum.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In today's world, the mental model of just going for postgraduate courses is a bit passé.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In many of these areas that are fast evolving, the best training is not in a postgraduate course.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The best training and the best exposure are actually with the leading-edge companies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, while postgraduate courses are important, we will continue to monitor whether we need to start a postgraduate course and have the critical mass to do so, and if there is a market demand to do so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At this point in time, it is still early days.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But what we should really do is to make sure that our aspiring e-sports gamers, designers or developers have the best opportunities to work with the best around the world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, getting them into companies to have the necessary exposure is important.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Member's second and third questions are related to how the Government should spend grants and who do we give the grants to, and should we interfere in the commercial arrangements between developers and some of these gaming houses.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Any entrepreneur who wants to start up a new business can obviously get various forms of help from the Government, but it will not be the appropriate role for the Government to pick and say that this is better done than another thing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, actually, the best test of where to apply the funds will certainly be the markets.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A good idea will always have opportunities with the venture capitalists and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Government agencies and the taxpayers' money should not be used to displace the market mechanism and the general workings of the market.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, anybody, be it in this particular sector or any other sector, if they would like to get help from the economic agencies, they can always contact Enterprise Singapore, they can always look at the various schemes that the Government has to help our companies to grow.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As to the Member's third question, that is best left to the commercial arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not possible, and neither do I think it is right, for the Government to intervene in the commercial arrangements between different companies and different games developers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I understand where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But there is a market mechanism that can work and I will be very careful to intervene to disrupt or displace the market mechanism.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I cannot help but also worry about the announcement that the World Health Organization made last year that has classified gaming disorder as a disease.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not exactly the same as the e-sports that we are talking about.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are talking about another part of the spectrum, which, of course, we are concerned about if there are such things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are also working with the schools to make sure that people who get involved in electronic games are properly guided and they maintain a certain sense of discipline, so that they do not get into trouble at all.
